sections.h2: Where the Register of Deeds is
sections.html:
The office is in Suite 200 at 800 Tenth Street in Baldwin, the county seat. The clerk and the register of deeds share it, so every deed for Lake County land goes across the same counter.

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:30 am until 5:00 pm
  • Friday: 8:30 am until 4:00 pm
  • Phone (231) 745-2725, fax (231) 745-8632

Equalization has its own suite at the same address, Suite 230, phone (231) 745-2723. It maintains property descriptions and helps with assessment questions.

Lake County is rural, seasonal and low priced. About 567 square miles of land hold an estimated 13,182 residents. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $133,900, and owners occupy 82.0% of homes. Of 13,315 housing units counted in 2020, 61.9% were vacant, and 28.6% of residents are 65 or older.

That vacancy share means many parcels sit empty for long stretches, so an owner selling one may live far from Baldwin. Call the office with the parcel number to learn what it needs before you mail anything.

Bring or mail a check, money order or cash to the clerk's office. Recording fees cannot be paid online. The county's web payment page covers copies, vital records and cremation permits, and the register of deeds page carves out recordable land record fees as the exception.

State law sets the amounts. Under MCL 600.2567 the charge is $30 per recorded document however many pages it runs, $1 per copied page, $5 to certify a recording, and a $5 floor on a records search. A discharge or assignment covering extra instruments adds $3 per instrument. A charter county may adopt another schedule, so phone the office to verify the total first.

Two layers apply, as elsewhere in Michigan. The county layer is 55 cents per $500 because Lake County has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). The state layer is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525).

Because the seller bears the tax, the instrument has to show the full value, or a valuation affidavit has to go with it. Any exemption has to be written on the deed.

The clerk's office sends back non-compliant instruments with a checklist, and the checklist cites the Michigan statute for each problem. Most are fixable before you submit.

  • Original ink signatures, with each name printed or typed below, matching the notary block.
  • A street number or post office address for every grantee.
  • The drafter's name and address.
  • One statement of the recordable event on line one of page one, in black ink, 10-point type or larger, over a 2.5 inch blank top margin (half an inch on the other margins).
  • Paper no smaller than letter size and no longer than legal.
  • At most four sequential digits of any Social Security number.
  • An attached English translation for any foreign-language text.

Other triggers include a survivor deed with no recorded death certificate, an uncertified court order, a trust document that is not recorded as its own instrument, and a missing date in the acknowledgment.

The Equalization Department posts them, and it is the first stop for questions that are not about recording. It runs annual sales and appraisal studies on every class of real property and uses them to equalize values across the county's 15 local units of government. State law (MCL 211.34) frames that work around an assessment level of 50% of true cash value.

Its page links to the state forms an owner is most likely to need: the principal residence exemption and homestead form, a request to rescind a PRE, the disabled veteran exemption, and the property transfer affidavit. It also links the Michigan Treasury property tax estimator, which lets you compare millage rates across local units. A seller can use that tool to show a buyer what the tax on the parcel is likely to look like.

Annual apportionment and equalization reports are posted on the same page, with years back to 2015 for apportionment, so a buyer or heir can see how values were adjusted from year to year.

sections.h2: Filing a deed from out of town
sections.html:
Many Lake County owners live elsewhere, so mail filing is common. Call (231) 745-2725 with your parcel number before you send anything, and ask whether the office sees any problem with the deed type you hold. Then confirm the total: $30 for recording, any $3 extras for added instruments, the transfer tax, and a separate certificate fee if the deed carries warranty covenants.

Send original signed paper only, with a check or money order, because fees cannot be paid online. If the office finds a problem, it returns the deed with the checklist, so build in time for a second mailing before your closing date. Keep a copy of everything you send.

The register of deeds runs a fraud alert program that notifies subscribers when land record activity matches their name. Mail your name, email, phone number, mailing address and parcel ID (if known) to Lake County Register of Deeds, Attn: Fraud Alert, 800 10th Street, Suite 200, Baldwin, Michigan 49304.

An owner who lives elsewhere and holds a cabin or vacant land can use the alert as an early warning that someone has recorded a document against the parcel. The same page links to online land record searches, which you can use to review a parcel's recorded deeds before a sale.

Deal with taxes first. A deed that carries warranty covenants will not record without the county treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135, which speaks to liens and the last five years of tax. Request it from the Lake County treasurer well ahead of closing.

Equalization covers the 15 local units and about 27,000 real property parcels, with permanent parcel numbers in use since 1987, so keep the number handy when you phone. After closing, the buyer has 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessing office (MCL 211.27a), and next year's taxable value is reset.

Whether the buyer finances or pays cash, the steps are the same. With a cash buyer there is usually no lender checklist on top of them, which can shorten the time between signing and recording.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Lake County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $30 for each recorded document, and a discharge or assignment that covers extra instruments costs $3 more per instrument. Take payment to the clerk's office as a check, money order or cash, since the online payment page excludes recording fees.

faqs.q: When can I visit the office?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday it runs 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and on Friday it closes at 4:00 pm. Go to Suite 200, 800 Tenth Street, Baldwin, or call (231) 745-2725.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Lake County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. Together the two rates are $4.30 per $500 of value, and a deed gets no exemption unless it says so on its face.

faqs.q: Why would the office return my deed?
faqs.a: Usually for a formatting or signature problem: no original signatures, no drafter name and address, a missing grantee address, the wrong margins or paper size, or no statement of total value. The office sends back a checklist of the reasons with the instrument.

faqs.q: Can I search Lake County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's page links to online land records and describes a fraud alert program you join by mail with your details and parcel ID.
